compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The MCP `review_plan` tool (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) derives whether it signs a plan-review
attestation SOLELY from server read-only mode: it calls the library with
`sign=not ro, emit_sidecar=not ro`. There is no caller-facing `sign` parameter, so an MCP
client cannot request an explicit unsigned review the way a CLI caller can with `--no-sign`
or a library caller can with `sign=False`. Conversely, when read-only mode DOES suppress
signing, the returned verdict carries no machine-readable reason saying so — a client sees an
unsigned PASS and cannot distinguish "policy suppressed the signature" from "signing failed".

Split out of epic 58f2-b6ed-363e-4608 (uninformed-aspiring-rhino) on 2026-07-24: the CLI and
library boundaries of that epic are a test/help-hardening job, while this is a genuine public
API change to a different boundary with tool-schema and generated-reference consequences.

## Expected Behavior
- MCP `review_plan` accepts `sign: bool = True`, matching the library default.
- An explicit `sign=False` runs the review without signing, and the result names the caller's
  opt-out as the unsigned reason.
- Read-only server mode continues to suppress signing regardless of the requested value, and
  the result carries a machine-readable unsigned reason identifying the read-only policy
  (distinct from the caller-opt-out reason and from a signing failure).
- The tool docstring states the sign-by-default contract and both unsigned exceptions.

## Approach
1. Add `sign: bool = True` to the MCP `review_plan` signature; pass `sign=sign and not ro`.
2. Introduce a machine-readable unsigned-reason field on the verdict distinguishing:
   `caller-opt-out`, `readonly-policy`, `not-signable` (BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/degraded/local),
   and `sign-failed`. Reuse the existing `signature.signed` boolean as the primary contract;
   the reason is additive, so existing consumers stay byte-compatible.
3. Update the tool docstring and regenerate `docs/mcp-reference.md`.

Rejected: inferring the reason client-side from the verdict shape — the read-only and
not-signable cases are indistinguishable without server knowledge, which is the bug.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (unsigned-reason plumbing, if the reason is
  produced at the finalization seam rather than the MCP boundary)
- MCP surface tests for plan review
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` (generated tool inventory / outputSchema)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] MCP `review_plan` exposes `sign: bool = True`; a contract test proves the default
      persists an attestation and `sign=False` does not.
- [ ] With `sign=False`, the result carries a machine-readable unsigned reason identifying the
      caller opt-out; a test asserts the exact reason value.
- [ ] In read-only mode the result is unsigned regardless of the requested `sign` value and
      carries the read-only-policy reason, distinct from the caller-opt-out reason; a
      table-driven test covers (sign x readonly) combinations.
- [ ] A never-signable verdict (BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / degraded / local source) reports the
      not-signable reason rather than the opt-out or read-only reason.
- [ ] The MCP tool docstring states sign-by-default and names both unsigned exceptions;
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` regenerates cleanly and matches.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
compiled_state.title: MCP review_plan has no caller-facing sign opt-out and no machine-readable unsigned reason
